label: Figure 1
title: Dollar thresholds in force since October 1, 2025, and the text that sets each
caption: Final rule 90 FR 41872 raised six thresholds on October 1, 2025 and left the bond, wage-rate and trade-agreements figures alone [340](#cite:340) [417](#cite:417). Each row gives the figure now in the text named, the figure it replaced where the rule states one, and the text that prints it. Where two official texts disagree the table gives both. 13 CFR 125.3 still prints $750,000 and $1,500,000 for subcontracting plans against $900,000 and $2 million in FAR 19.702 [704](#cite:704) [692](#cite:692). 13 CFR 124.506 prints $7,000,000, $4,500,000 and $25,000,000 for 8(a) awards against $8.5 million, $5.5 million and $30 million in the FAR [331](#cite:331) [338](#cite:338) [339](#cite:339). 10 U.S.C. 3702 reads $10,000,000 for defense prime contracts entered into after June 30, 2026, against $2.5 million in FAR 15.403-4 [1036](#cite:1036) [1325](#cite:1325). Construction bonds start above $150,000 in the FAR and above $100,000 in the statute as read [644](#cite:644) [947](#cite:947). Other dollar gates, such as the $25,000 notice line [562](#cite:562) and the trafficking compliance plan [654](#cite:654), are in the gate records and are not repeated here.
how_to_read: Read across a row: the threshold, the figure in force, the figure before October 1, 2025, and the text that prints it. Where you see the same threshold on two rows, two official texts disagree; the status column tells you whether one text lags, or whether the second figure applies only to defense contracts. A blank in the prior column means the references read do not state an earlier figure. It does not mean there was none. The governing text named in each row is where the figure is printed.

explain.text: The figure was changed by the inflation-adjustment rule, FAR Case 2024-001, published August 27, 2025 and effective October 1, 2025 [417](#cite:417) [340](#cite:340).

Two official texts print different figures for the same threshold. The table shows both and does not pick one. For subcontracting plans and the 8(a) figures the second text is an SBA regulation in Title 13 [704](#cite:704) [331](#cite:331).

The rule names these thresholds as left out of the adjustment: Construction Wage Rate Requirements, Service Contract Labor Standards, performance and payment bonds, and trade agreements [340](#cite:340).

explain.text: A later change in statute for defense contracts. Section 1804(c) of Pub. L. 119-60 raised the figure to $10,000,000 for prime contracts entered into after June 30, 2026; $2,000,000 applies on or before that date [1036](#cite:1036).
The published figure written out as a whole number of dollars so that rows can be sorted and drawn. "$8.5 million" becomes 8500000. Nothing else was converted.

source: Values are as published in the Federal Register rule, the codified FAR (FAC 2026-01), the eCFR text of 13 CFR and the U.S. Code as read on October 1 to 4, 2026; each row names its text and carries its reference numbers. The amount_usd and prior_usd columns restate the published figure as an integer; no inflation adjustment or other conversion was made. The script draws the table as a before-and-after chart on a log scale.
